questions.worked_solution:
The range of $\sqrt[6]{x}$ is

$$
\sqrt[6]{x}\ge 0.
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches do not affect the range. Hence,

$$
\sqrt[6]{2-3x}\ge 0.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $-3,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[6]{2-3x} & \ge 0 \\ -3\sqrt[6]{2-3x} & \le 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the range of the given function is $f(x)\in (-\infty ,0].$

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown below.

Example: 
                    Finding the Range of a Transformed Radical Function With an Even Index
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The range of $\sqrt[4] x$ is

$$
\sqrt[4] x \ge 0.
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches do not affect the range. Therefore,

$$
\sqrt[4]{1-2x} \ge 0.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $-2$ and then adding $1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[4]{1-2x} & \ge 0 \\ -2\sqrt[4]{1-2x} & \le 0 \\ -2\sqrt[4]{1-2x}+1 & \le 1 \\ f(x) & \le 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the range of the given function is $f(x) \in (-\infty,1].$

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249143/assets/3ce03253fe40abe25d69866d5b52a621168e3dab2a45ca33d951f1a4551b98c9.png)

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
The range of a radical function $f(x)=\sqrt[n]{x}$ depends on whether the index $n$ of the radical is even or odd. 

Let's start with the odd case first. What is the range of 

$$
f(x) = -2\sqrt[3]{3x-2}+2?
$$

First, recall that the range of $y = \sqrt[3] x$ is
$y \in (-\infty,\infty).$

Transformations do not change this interval. Therefore, the range of $f(x)$ is $y \in (-\infty,\infty).$

Let's start with the odd case first. What is the range of 

$$
f(x) = -2\sqrt[3]{3x-2}+2?
$$

First, recall that the range of $y = \sqrt[3] x$ is
$y \in (-\infty,\infty).$

Transformations do not change this interval. Therefore, the range of $f(x)$ is $y \in (-\infty,\infty).$

tutorials.name: The Range of a Transformed Radical Function With an Even Index
tutorials.problem:
Let's now focus on the even case. What is the range of 

$$
g(x) = -3\sqrt[4]{2x-1}-2?
$$

The range of $\sqrt[4] x$ is

$$
\sqrt[4] x \ge 0.
$$

Now, let's apply transformations to the inequality above to turn the left-hand side into $g(x).$

First, remember that horizontal shifts and stretches do not affect the range. Therefore,

$$
\sqrt[4]{2x-1} \ge 0.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $-3$ and then subtracting $2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[4]{2x-1} & \ge 0 \\ -3\sqrt[4]{2x-1} & \le 0 \\ -3\sqrt[4]{2x-1}-2 & \le -2 \\ g(x) & \le -2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the range of the given function is $g(x) \in (-\infty,-2].$

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=g(x)$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249143/assets/1b7f3dc07cb72ea087d7cc4ec01379efa212b89fb8ab397b6df5bccfe75e66f5.png)
